sourceDoc.text:
Endovascular or open repair strategy for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm: 30 
day outcomes from IMPROVE randomised trial.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether a strategy of endovascular repair (if aortic 
morphology is suitable, open repair if not) versus open repair reduces early 
mortality for patients with suspected ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
DESIGN: Randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: 30 vascular centres (29 UK, 1 Canadian), 2009-13.
PARTICIPANTS: 613 eligible patients (480 men) with a clinical diagnosis of 
ruptured aneurysm.
INTERVENTIONS: 316 patients were randomised to the endovascular strategy (275 
confirmed ruptures, 174 anatomically suitable for endovascular repair) and 297 
to open repair (261 confirmed ruptures).
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: 30 day mortality, with 24 hour and in-hospital mortality, 
costs, and time and place of discharge as secondary outcomes.
RESULTS: 30 day mortality was 35.4% (112/316) in the endovascular strategy group 
and 37.4% (111/297) in the open repair group: odds ratio 0.92 (95% confidence 
interval 0.66 to 1.28; P=0.62); odds ratio after adjustment for age, sex, and 
Hardman index 0.94 (0.67 to 1.33). Women may benefit more than men (interaction 
test P=0.02) from the endovascular strategy: odds ratio 0.44 (0.22 to 0.91) 
versus 1.18 (0.80 to 1.75). 30 day mortality for patients with confirmed rupture 
was 36.4% (100/275) in the endovascular strategy group and 40.6% (106/261) in 
the open repair group (P=0.31). More patients in the endovascular strategy than 
in the open repair group were discharged directly to home (189/201 (94%) v 
141/183 (77%); P<0.001). Average 30 day costs were similar between the 
randomised groups, with an incremental cost saving for the endovascular strategy 
versus open repair of £1186 (€1420; $1939) (95% confidence interval -£625 to 
£2997).
CONCLUSIONS: A strategy of endovascular repair was not associated with 
significant reduction in either 30 day mortality or cost. Longer term cost 
effectiveness evaluations are needed to assess the full effects of the 
endovascular strategy in both men and women.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Current Controlled Trials ISRCTN48334791.

recordedTake.finding: An endovascular-first strategy for suspected ruptured AAA showed no statistically clear difference in day mortality compared with open repair.
recordedTake.designCaution: This is a strategy trial in which only part of the endovascular arm was anatomically suitable for endovascular repair, so it does not isolate the effect of the device itself, and the apparent benefit in women comes from a subgroup interaction that is hypothesis-generating at best.
recordedTake.relevance: A landmark RCT directly informing your AAA/TAAA outcomes north star, with a useful pragmatic strategy-trial design for rupture pathways.

check.reason: The snippet reports 30-day mortality of 35.4% vs 37.4% with P=0.62 and odds ratio including 1.0, explicitly stating 'no significant reduction,' which matches the claim of no statistically clear difference.

cautionCheck.reason: The snippet confirms this was a strategy trial (endovascular 'if suitable, open repair if not'), reports only 174 of 316 endovascular patients were anatomically suitable, and explicitly notes the female benefit came from an interaction test (P=0.02) without claiming clinical significance, supporting both design limitations stated in the claim.
